Apple today said that a new UK proposal targeting App Store fees amounts to price regulation, warning it could harm innovation and investment. Details below.

Apple pushes back against App Store regulation in the UK

According to Reuters, Apple today filed a formal response to a consultation by the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), opposing a proposed rule that would let app developers link to alternative payment methods.

The CMA has already designated Apple and Google as having "strategic market status" in their respective mobile platforms, which allows it to impose tailored requirements. Under the UK's new digital markets regime, this designation enables the regulator to introduce company-specific rules to foster competition and give consumers more choice.

Under the proposal, Apple and Google could still take a commission on transactions completed by developers via alternative payment methods, but any such fee must be considered "fair and reasonable".

Reuters noted that the CMA "expects guided fees to be lower than current app store charges and that the savings would be passed on to UK consumers or reinvested in developers' businesses to support innovation".

Apple, however, takes a very different view and is opposing the proposal. Reuters reports:

同

The CMA has rejected Apple's characterisation of the proposal as price regulation, saying its intent is to set principles for judging whether guided fees are fair and reasonable, not to set fee levels directly.
